data.title: Rapamycin across biology and medicine: From molecular mechanisms to clinical and translational frontiers
data.authors: Nolasco LNRA; de Vargas Wolfgramm Dos Santos E; Dos Reis Trabach RS; Meira DD; Louro ID
data.journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta, General Subjects

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Comprehensive review tracing rapamycin from its discovery as an antifungal macrolide to its identification as the founding mTOR inhibitor. Covers mTOR's role integrating nutrient/growth-factor/stress signals, established and emerging clinical applications of rapamycin/rapalogs, limitations and adverse effects of mTOR inhibition, and translational prospects for using mTOR inhibition to prevent or delay chronic disease and extend healthspan.
data.abstract_excerpt: Rapamycin is a macrolide compound originally identified for its antifungal activity and subsequently recognized as a potent inhibitor of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR), a conserved signaling kinase that integrates nutrient availability, growth factor signals, and cellular stress responses to regulate cell growth and metabolism. This review examines rapamycin across biological and medical fields, covering its discovery, chemical and pharmacological properties, and the central role of mTOR as its primary molecular target.

extracted_findings.intervention: none (narrative review of rapamycin and rapalogs)
extracted_findings.species: not applicable (review spanning preclinical and clinical literature)
extracted_findings.effect: Argues that mTOR inhibition is a unifying strategy across chronic disease and healthspan, while setting out the limitations and adverse effects of the approach.
